principles.statement: Treat ASR as a fallible sensor, not an authority: machine recognition is evidence about one model's response to speech, not direct proof of learner capability.
Never infer pronunciation correctness from successful transcription alone and never infer mispronunciation from non-recognition alone.
Do not use raw WER, MER, transcript confidence or n-best position as a pronunciation mastery score.
Keep machine transcription success, feature-level pronunciation evidence, human intelligibility and comprehensibility as separate evidence dimensions.
Before automating corrective feedback, validate the detector on the exact pronunciation feature, learner population and task family it will judge.
Use Vietnamese population ASR disparities as a reason for stronger calibration and uncertainty handling, not as evidence that an individual learner speaks poorly.
Log ASR provider/model/version, language/accent configuration, prompt/task type, expected text or intent, audio conditions and scoring rule with every machine-derived attempt.
A model validated on read speech cannot silently become the judge of guided or spontaneous speech; each task shift requires evidence of generalization.
Prefer ASR for low-stakes candidate detection, transcript assistance and practice feedback before using it for consequential gates.
For phoneme, stress, rhythm or intonation feedback, require a feature-specific validated detector or measurement rather than pretending ordinary ASR directly measures the feature.
When machine signals disagree or confidence falls into an unvalidated region, return uncertainty, request another sample or defer judgment instead of inventing a precise score.
Calibrate automated feedback against human listener outcomes that match Nếp's intelligibility-first goal, not only native-model acoustic distance.
ASR-based practice can be offered when it helps learners attempt and notice pronunciation, while its learning benefit remains separate from the validity of its scores.
Version automated evidence so historical learner records can be reinterpreted after model changes or recalibration.

A machine-derived pronunciation signal may contribute to mastery only after product validation establishes acceptable error and bias under the intended Vietnamese near-A0 conditions; until then it remains supporting evidence only.
